## The terminal session stays a terminal, including the defects the notebook cut is required to close.

The terminal is preserved. The notebook must not regress a raw login, the paged restore, the splits, the commands, the formatters, or the account file. Cleaning those up to make the thread lanes prettier is refused.

The width contract is this. The shell sends terminal columns and rows on connect and on every pane resize, using the window-change the SSH stack already has. The host listens and updates the terminal width and the reply format context. Input redraw wraps at that width with the ordinary carriage return and line discipline, consistent with the server formatters. If no size arrives, the width stays the environment width or eighty columns, and that is treated as normal. There is no second wrap protocol. The earlier defect was a width captured once, defaulting to eighty, and never updated. The contract is the update, not the freeze.

The idle contract is this. The client idle timeout is configurable on the client connection file `~/.casserole/ssh-client.yaml`. The default is never disconnect. Zero means disabled. The session stays up until the operator disconnects or exits. An idle kick on the order of ten minutes, about 600000 milliseconds, is a library default and a defect, not the product. The server does not idle-kick an operator session on that same default. The server side is configurable, and its default is disabled for an operator SSH session. The first plan's client file was the older properties file `~/.ssh-client.properties`, and that plan refused to merge it into the product file. The notebook lock names the YAML file under `~/.casserole/`. The Rust client reads that YAML file and, when it is missing, may import the older properties file once. The product file and the connection file stay two files.

Command mode is a toggle that stays. Escape from chat or from idle enters command mode and remains there until Escape again. Commands run inside command mode. A successful command does not bounce back to chat, except exit, and except an explicit chat command that is the operator's way back. Empty Enter in command mode reprints the command prompt. The welcome text says that Escape toggles command mode. The bare Escape toggle stays. The defect was the bounce after a command, not the toggle itself. The chat prompt is `chat>`. The command prompt is `cmd>`.

The host's thinking spinner is preserved with the terminal. Its default form is the plain glyph, with a braille form only when the font has the glyphs, and a form that draws nothing. The interval and the colors of that spinner are terminal format, owned by the server format page. This map only refuses to drop the spinner when the notebook arrives, and refuses to log a burner while tracing payloads.

A clean hangup that commits still restores. The account file `users.yaml` still authenticates. When that file is present it is the source of truth for accounts. The framed protocol is not wrapped around a raw OpenSSH login.

**Truth.** The terminal remains a VT100 session with its own memory, its own prompts, and its own interrupt. Width follows the pane. Idle defaults to stay up. Escape stays in command mode until Escape again. Raw logins stay raw. The notebook is not allowed to regress any of that.

**Reason.** The terminal was the product before the notebook, and operators already depend on it. A frozen width and a ten-minute kick were defects in that preservation, so they are closed in the same cut that opens the notebook, without becoming canvas features. Command mode that bounces after every command is not a mode.

**Avoidances.** Do not invent a second wrap protocol. Do not idle-kick at ten minutes by default. Do not return to chat after an ordinary command. Do not merge the connection file into the product file. Do not wrap a raw login in frames. Do not reparent the terminal widget. Do not let canvas work delay these terminal repairs, and do not let the repairs become an excuse to skip the notebook.

## The languages are JDK 26 for both Java programs and idiomatic Rust for the second client, and every source file carries the notice.

The Java server and the Java shell build and run on JDK 26. The compiler and the runtime match. The JDK is Azul Zulu 26. It is not another vendor's kit. The project property `java.version` is 26. The first plan recorded the Boot parent it found as 3.5.0 and said to keep it unless 26 would not compile, in which case the build stops and asks. The later ledger of what that build delivered names parent 3.5.16 and an explicit start class. The same ledger says the first Boot line that lists this JDK is not a silent upgrade, and that a packaging failure while the bytecode scanner still sees major 70, until the start class is explicit, is a stop-and-ask, not a quiet jump. Both writings stand. The present parent the ledger names is 3.5.16. The plan's stop-and-ask still binds. Spring AI 1.1.8 is the model library the first plan was watching on that JDK. Server adapters may sit in front of that library. The shell does not boot the server.

The fetched runtime lives at `~/.aetheris/jre/zulu-26`. The directory name says `jre`. The bits inside are a JDK, because the compiler is required, and the path is not renamed. The first plan preferred a JRE download and allowed the full kit only if a JRE could not satisfy the compiler. The delivered fetch is the JDK in that JRE-named directory. Scripts that find `JAVA_HOME` already on 26 inherit it. Otherwise they set `JAVA_HOME` and `PATH` to the fetched runtime and override any other Java for that script run.

Types the project owns stay in ordinary Java. Accessor code is written out. A framework annotation processor is not added for that. A code-generation library for accessors is refused. Lambdas are not the default in project types. Named types carry the work. Virtual threads are not used. The lanes are ordinary Java threads through a pool executor. Virtual threads remain a refused alternative unless a later lock accepts them. A comment that only repeats a parameter name does not carry the why. A Java comment carries the class prose. Documentation that a reader needs sits with the type. A diagram belongs where an executor's states are not obvious. The author of the notice is the author on the types.

The Rust client stays idiomatic Rust. Module prose is `//!`. Item prose is `///`. The tag sits with that prose. The window pair is egui on winit. The vault engine is Turso. The SSH library stays behind the host side of the terminal core. The grid the operator sees is this client's grid. A Rust comment carries the module prose.

Logging is Log4j2 on both Java processes. Logback is excluded. The configuration files are properties files, not XML. The application configuration stays YAML. Annotation support for the logger is required. The server properties file is `log4j2.properties`. It writes a console appender and a file at `~/.casserole/logs/casserole.log`, creating the parent directory on first write. The shell properties file is `log4j2-shell.properties`. The root level is INFO. The loggers `org.casserole`, `org.roux`, and `org.apache.sshd` are tunable. The pattern carries timestamp, level, thread, logger, and message. The shell file is `~/.aetheris/logs/aetheris-shell.log`, file only, at INFO, so a window is not spammed. The shell configures that file before the interface starts. INFO is low chatter: start, stop, listen port, authentication source, exclusive refusal. DEBUG is useful and is not a full prompt. TRACE may log payloads and must never log a burner payload. The rule is written before burners exist. The server start keeps one console line so an operator still sees the port. The helper class is `org.casserole.log.CasseroleLog`, using the logger manager, with a get by class and a get by name. The product name in About and Help becomes Aetheris Shell where those strings are the product name. The host name, the memory name, and the `chat>` prompt are not renamed. The menu reads as About Aetheris.

The server lanes are three live lanes. The enum tokens are `SSH_IO`, `LLM_EXEC`, and `GENERAL`. The same lanes are also named `ssh-io`, `llm-exec`, and `general`. Metrics exist and default off. The host key is `casserole.lamina.metrics`, default false. A true value may turn them on. When they are on they are log-tail counts of submit, complete, fail, and wait. They are not an external telemetry stack. Pool sizes are code defaults when the file omits them. The tool lane and a memory-IO lane are named `TOOL_EXEC` and `ROUX_IO`, and also `tool-exec` and `roux-io`, and they are not given pools until a cut needs them. Cell execution in the notebook cut uses `LLM_EXEC`. The listen loop is a task on the terminal input lane. The server accept type is not itself a thread. The per-connection read loop is a task on that same lane. The model completion is a task on the model lane. Destroy cancels those handles. Escape and spinner timers stay timers. The SSH library's processor threads stay library-owned. An unused web container is not migrated into the lanes. Client threads are not lanes: the file-send worker, the connect worker, and the interface event thread. After the move, the server path does not construct a raw thread or a raw executor, apart from the terminal client package and the leftover types that were ordered left alone. Shutdown drains through the lanes.

The first build does not add a test framework unless a change asks. The later rule is that where a test already covers the behavior, that test is updated in the same change, in the form the repository already uses. Both stand. Unasked new framework use is still refused. An existing test is not left stale.

Every source file carries the copyright notice as the first comment on the page. One notice covers the classes and the modules on the page. A blank line ends the notice. The prose of the type follows. The year is the year that file first carries the notice. The source filed with the product constitution uses 2026. The permission notice is the MIT License file distributed with the project. A use keeps the copyright notice and that permission notice. A modification keeps them too. A new source file carries the notice. The notice text is this.

```
Copyright (c) 2026 Clay Lambert <the.sovereign.systems.architect@gmail.com>
All rights reserved.

Author: Clay Lambert

Licensed under the MIT License.
If you use or modify this source, you must include this copyright notice
and the MIT License permission notice in all copies or substantial portions
of the software, including modifications.
```

How a change keeps the program is part of the same language contract. Before a change, read the prose and the specification the work names. New behavior is named in the specification, with the why, before the code. A behavior change updates the specification, the prose, and the code together. A type the change does not touch keeps its prose. Neighboring blocks stay. A tag uses an identifier this repository already defines, then the specification file, then a heading when the type has one. A tag written as a spec-colon prefix is refused. A type with no heading gains one on the specification that owns the concern. The repository keeps one index of live specification heads. An open page grows in blocks. The earlier words stay. A frozen serial stays filed, and the next serial becomes the head. A comment carries the design reason. A private name, a private path, a host that is not the published local endpoint, a password, a real key, and a shop ritual stay out. This map carries the published ports and the published endpoints because the product's public configuration is part of the contract, not because a private address was copied in.

A heading carries one decision block after its prose: the truth that stands, the reason that shape won, and the avoidances that still guard the design. When the truth moves, the block is written again as a whole. The chronology stays off the published page. The why absorbs the history.

A specification update is additive. A published page keeps every detail it already carries. An update adds. A page is not scaled down, and it is not stripped, unless a removal is approved and the approval names the cut. Size is not a cap. Silence is not a cap. A percentage named on one ask is the cap for that ask only. Documentation, in the repository notes and in the source, is full at the scale of the behavior. The speech is for engineers and for operators. The code is the representation of that prose.

A comment bridge on new Java may name a key the repository already has. It is not a second requirements catalog. A vector store, a case tool, and an extra syntax parser are refused as the way to check that bridge. Old types stay untagged until the file is touched. An unresolved question still blocks a plan. A tag does not close it. English remains the prime text. The sweep that shames a dangling tag is a later hygiene, not a gate on the notebook.

**Truth.** Both Java programs are JDK 26 on Azul Zulu, parent 3.5.16 as the ledger records it, with a stop if that line will not build. Rust is idiomatic, egui on winit, Turso for the vault. Log4j2 replaces Logback on both Java processes. Every source file starts with the 2026 MIT notice naming Clay Lambert. Accessors are written out. Threads are ordinary threads on three live lanes.

**Reason.** One JDK for the compiler and the runtime removes a class of "it built there" failures. A named runtime vendor keeps the scripts pointed at a kit that is actually fetched. The notice is how a stranger knows the license without a separate oral tradition. Ordinary threads and written accessors keep the code readable on the same terms as the prose. The Rust client's missing or unusable port key is 2222, and the usable range it accepts is 1 through 65535. A stored Rust port wins, including 22. Both clients, when the host key is missing, use `localhost`. The Rust client's missing username is the operating-system user. Remembered secrets are not written on this page. The password field is empty unless the operator has chosen to remember it, and even then the value stays off the page.

A missing Java font size is 20. The key the Java client uses is `ui.terminal.font.size`. A missing or unreadable Rust font size is 14. The published code model is `qwen2.5-coder:7b`. It is the host chat model and the host chat-options model, and those two stay the same string. The published pull strategy is `never`, so startup does not download a model. The operator pulls the model out of band. Startup still succeeds when the local engine is down.

`num-ctx` is the local engine's context window, not the terminal transcript cap. A code value of 0 omits the field. A negative value omits it as well. An omitted field means the engine uses the model's own window. A positive integer is sent as the engine's context option on a chat request, on a load, and on the load half of a swap. The published example is 8192. That example is the public sample. It is not a private override, and this page does not publish a private override. The remote call does not grow a second copy of this field inside a cell.

The remote URL is `https://api.x.ai/v1/chat/completions`. The key placeholder is `your-grok-api-key`. That string is not a key. A real key is not written here, not written in a cell, and not written in a log. The air-gap sample in the product file is false. True refuses a cloud target without changing the stored target.

The Java theme defaults named with the notebook are the cursor, the inactive cursor, the menu font, the terminal foreground, the chat prompt, and the command prompt, as the canvas section states them. The idle timeout default is 0, meaning disabled. The inspector wrap width default is 80 when a saved character width is used. The terminal column default when no size arrives is 80. The vault pool maximum in the sample is 4. The footer mock's maximum-tokens spinner shows 100. The keepalive idle is 2 seconds. The writer wait does not fail at 50 milliseconds. The payload cap is 1 MiB.

No LAN address, no password, and no private model name belong on this page. `localhost` and the public API host above are the published endpoints, not a private network.

The code model is `qwen2.5-coder:7b` at `http://localhost:11434`. Zero `num-ctx` omits the field. The published example is 8192. ## A start installs dependencies, then starts.

Every start script installs every dependency, then starts. The scripts assume nothing is installed. A person who knows nothing gets a clean startup of the server and of both clients. The scripts are built so a failed step stops the start. A dependency that is already valid stays. A failed download stops before the program starts, and the message names the next command.

The scripts live in `bin/` at the repository root. They exist for Windows, in the three Windows script forms, and for Linux and macOS in the same bash. The script names are `casserole`, `aetheris-shell`, `fetch-zulu-jre`, `install-ollama`, and `bootstrap-env`. A helper named `_java` resolves Java for the others. The shell classpath is built by `LocalM2Classpath` from `~/.m2`. If nothing beyond the fetched JDK and the local engine is required, the bootstrap says so and exits success. It does not invent a package-manager stack. Linux stays flavor-agnostic. A distribution package manager appears only inside the engine's own installer if that vendor script needs it. The engine installer is idempotent when the engine is already on the path. The runtime fetch is idempotent when the fetched `java` is already 26. It fails loudly when the address or the hash is wrong.

Java resolution is this. If `JAVA_HOME` is set and the reported version is 26, inherit it. Else if `~/.aetheris/jre/zulu-26/` exists, point `JAVA_HOME` and `PATH` at it and override any other Java. Else tell the operator to run the fetch and exit nonzero.

The server script defaults to the build tool's run goal, with the resolved Java. An optional jar flag, if a packaged jar already exists, runs that jar. If the jar is missing, the script says to package first and exits. It does not build a second start stack. The first plan's preference for a jar-first start was answered by keeping the build-tool start as the default and the jar as an optional flag. The later ledger keeps that default and refuses a third runner. If packaging fails its bytecode scan, stop and ask. Do not upgrade the Boot line to get past it.

The shell script launches `org.casserole.app.ui.ssh.SshClientApp` with `java` and a classpath built from the local dependency store. It passes through arguments, including `--aetheris-yaml`. It does not start the server. It never uses the build tool's exec goal. The first plan named that exec goal. The later ledger forbids it. Present start: the classpath. The shell can start without a network package index. The server script does not start the shell.

Operator scripts default to the local machine. The network is for the model engines, not for booting. Each script family has a readable note beside the scripts, with a table of arguments, readable in a plain pager, updated when the script changes.

Acceptance of the first build, which the later cuts are not allowed to undo, is this. The server listens on 2222 and the account file works. A raw login on that port still has chat, command mode, the spinner, the formatters, the message list, and the restore banner. A second disk-backed login as the same user is refused when durability commits. Hot-only still allows more than one in-memory session. The shell still connects, splits, opens and closes panes, pastes, and sends a file. A clean committed hangup still restores. The host still starts when the local engine is down, and a chat turn shows the error. Logging is Log4j2, with files under the two log directories named above. The title reads Aetheris Shell. There is no framed wrapping on a raw login, no canvas tab, and no vault file, in that first build alone. The notebook cut adds the tab, the frames, and the vault without breaking the first ten behaviors that are terminal behaviors.

The lanes are part of start. Metrics default off. The three live lanes exist before a client connects. The host is useful with no client vault.

**Truth.** Start means install, then run. The server starts through the build tool by default, with an optional jar. The shell starts through `java` and the local classpath, and never through the exec goal. Neither starts the other. A failed fetch stops the start and names the next command. The first build's raw terminal still has to pass after every later cut.

**Reason.** A script that assumes a kit is already installed is not a start for the person the product claims to serve. Separating the server start from the shell start is the same refusal as "a client does not start the server," written as a command. Keeping the raw-login acceptance in force is how the notebook is prevented from eating the terminal.

**Avoidances.** Do not start the server from the shell script. Do not use the exec goal for the shell. Do not require a network package index to open the window. Do not continue after a failed download. Do not replace a valid dependency. Do not invent a third server runner. Do not let a later cut drop the raw-login acceptance. Do not treat the first build's "no vault yet" as the present product. The vault arrives with the notebook, on the client, defaulting to disk.

1. This map, the shared contract.
2. `wire-amwp.md`, the frame.
3. `casserole-server.md`, the Java host.
4. `casserole-server-format.md`, the terminal presentation on that host.
5. `casserole-server-models.md`, the one model door.
6. `casserole-server-roux.md`, the two memories on the host.
7. `aetheris-java-shell.md`, the Java window around the terminal.
8. `aetheris-java-canvas.md`, the Java notebook.
9. `aetheris-rust-term.md`, the Rust terminal core.
10. `aetheris-rust-client.md`, the Rust program and its vault.
11. `aetheris-rust-chrome.md`, the Rust window surface.

A marker ledger is a separate shelf. This map does not rebuild it. The behavior of a silo is on the part page. A surface may differ. The wire may not.

It does not build a server loop or a window.

`casserole-server.md` builds the Java host as the reference: the SSH listen, the raw terminal when Init fails, the lanes, the accept path that is not itself a thread, the preservation of login and accounts, the refusal to open a client vault, the refusal to start a client, and the start script's server half. `casserole-server-format.md` builds what the terminal shows: prompts, sticky command mode, width and wrap, the spinner, formatters including the preserved JSON reply path, colors the server names, and the rule that canvas frames never become terminal bytes. It does not build a cell.

`casserole-server-models.md` builds the one provider door, the local engine, the published model and base, the `num-ctx` rule that zero omits the field, the swap command, the air-gap failure that does not rewrite a target, the engine-down failure, the burner-to-cloud refusal, and the remote URL as a later target on that same door. `casserole-server-roux.md` builds the two host memories: the terminal pack with one disk writer and the exclusive lock when the session is disk-backed, the hot-only exception, the canvas projection in memory under the dot-form identifier, the full replace on execute, the discard on reconnect, and the refusal of a second writer and of a multi-writer page protocol. `aetheris-java-canvas.md` builds the Swing notebook: canvases, cells, the four states, the burner pin, assembly, the inspector, the Java vault at its disk default, the shell executor for JDBC, and the version-1 export. # The mux is a little-endian frame of magic `0xAE` version 1, at most 1 MiB, on three channels, and a failed init leaves a raw terminal.

Packages: `org.aetheris.wire` for the text encoding and the frame codec. The host mux sits beside the chat shell. The facade is in the notebook package. The implementation may sit with the existing secure-shell input-output.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Magic / version | `0xAE` / `1` |
| Endian | little-endian |
| Maximum | 1 MiB, with the fragment flag on bit 2 |
| Channels | `0x0001` terminal, `0x0002` notebook, `0x0003` stream. Not `0x0004` |

The client demuxes bytes in front of the terminal connector's reader. The terminal widget sees only the terminal scope. The mux stream is not decoded as characters before the split.

The host mux wraps the chat shell's pipes. A client init that gets no valid reply stays a raw terminal. The terminal widget is never wrapped in that case.

An execute frame is length-prefixed. The body is the text encoding and carries the working set, `cell_id`, `execution_target`, and the knobs. One execute is in flight per `cell_id`. Cancel is best-effort on the existing completion handle.

`ssh -p 2222` must remain a raw terminal. If the init handshake fails, fall back to raw. Do not brick the operator tab.

A payload over 1 MiB is refused. The fragment bit is how a legal payload is split, not a way past the maximum.

**Truth.** Magic `0xAE`, version 1, little-endian, 1 MiB maximum, channels `0x0001`, `0x0002`, and `0x0003`, byte demux in front of the reader, and raw fallback when init fails.

**Reason.** The terminal widget must see only terminal bytes or its screen fills with frame noise. OpenSSH has no init, so it must stay the raw terminal it is today.

**Avoidances.** Do not decode the mux as characters before the split. Do not use channel `0x0004`. Do not wrap the terminal widget when init has no valid reply. Do not accept a payload over 1 MiB.

- The connection strip stays collapsed on a frame resize while connected.
- Mux: magic `0xAE`, little-endian, 1 MiB maximum, channels for the terminal, the notebook, and the stream. Init, or else a raw terminal. Bytes are demuxed in front of the character reader.
- Execute payload: a length-prefixed envelope, body in the text encoding inside `org.aetheris.wire`. One in-flight execute per `cell_id`.
- Client vault: HikariCP and H2 at compile scope on the shell. Pure JDBC and SQL constants. No persistence framework, no migration tool, and no Spring datasource on the host.
- A shell worker runs JDBC and client mux input-output off the event thread.
- Schema version 1: `workspace`, `canvas`, `cell`, `trace`. Disk path `~/.aetheris/{user}/vault`. Default `ram`. Disk is opt-in.
- The hand yaml reader grows `vault.mode`, `vault.path`, `network.air-gap`, and `amwp.enabled`. Spaces only. No second yaml library unless the hand parser is actually blocked, and then the builder stops.
- Four-state modal cells, a ghost that is the excluded visual, and a burner pin. Completing turn N materializes turn N+1. No scope table.
- Client working-set assembly, an inspector preview, and a token estimate. Execute pushes the full set into the RAM region.
- `openRam(sanitize(user) + ".aetheris")`. No file lock. No spill directory for that user. No dual write.
- Component scan includes `org.aetheris`.
- Cell execute runs on the existing model lane. Cancel is best-effort, the same as Ctrl+C on the operator terminal. No reactive stream type.
- Provider interface. Only the local engine is wired. A per-cell model dropdown. Operator command `swap <from> <to>`.
- Wrap and window size: columns on connect and on resize. The chat shell updates `terminalColumns`. The input line wraps. This row is critical.
- Client idle defaults to never disconnect. The host must not kick an operator session at 600 seconds.
- Sticky `cmd>`: Escape toggles and stays. No return to chat after commands, except `exit` and `chat start`.
- Theme keys: cursor, inactive cursor, menu foreground, green `chat>`, blue `cmd>`.
- Window icon: Eye of Horus crossed with a swoosh, green, blue, and gold on black.
- Scripts stay able to run offline. Script notes carry argument tables.
- `// @aa-sdd` on new Stage 1 types and methods, using the keys that already exist. No new catalog.

The local engine is `http://localhost:11434`. The code model default is `qwen2.5-coder:7b`. A context length of 0 omits `num_ctx`.

# The mux is an opaque byte split in front of the reader, the body is length-prefixed text, and cancel is best-effort.

- Cancel is best-effort through the existing completion handle.

Magic is `0xAE`, version 1, little-endian. Channels are `0x0001`, `0x0002`, and `0x0003`. Channel `0x0004` is not opened. The fragment flag is bit 2.

The terminal widget sees only the terminal scope. A client init with no valid reply does not wrap that widget.

OpenSSH on port 2222 stays raw.

**Truth.** Byte demux, opaque terminal scope, length-prefixed body, 1 MiB maximum, one in-flight execute per cell, and best-effort cancel.

**Reason.** A character-level demux corrupts the frame. A second in-flight execute for the same cell interleaves two answers into one card.

**Avoidances.** Do not decode the mux as characters before the split. Do not exceed 1 MiB. Do not open channel `0x0004`. Do not wrap the widget when init fails.

# The client does not start the host, the listener is port 2222, and a down engine still lets the host boot.

Two processes. The client is `SshClientApp`, Swing and JediTerm, package `org.casserole.app.ui.ssh`. It does not start the host framework. The host is `CasseroleApplication`, the host framework plus MINA. Each connection gets a `ChatShell`. Password authentication sits between them. The host calls `ChatModel.call`. The engine listens on port 11434 for local models. The public base is `http://localhost:11434`.

- Server: `mvn spring-boot:run`, then `CasseroleApplication`, then `InitRunner`, then `org.casserole.ssh.shell.SshServer.start()`.
- Client: run `org.casserole.app.ui.ssh.SshClientApp` from the IDE. Connect to `localhost:2222`.
- A plain client also works: `ssh -p 2222` to `localhost`, using the configured username and password. No password value is published. No account name is published.

If the engine is down, the host still starts. Chat turns print a red error. The listener is independent of the model.

**Truth.** Client and host are separate. Port 2222. A down engine still boots. Chat errors are red.

**Reason.** The listener must not depend on the model process being up.

**Avoidances.** Do not start the host framework from the client. Do not publish the password. Do not refuse boot when the engine is down.

Resources:

- `src/main/resources/application.properties`, empty.

# The log records the choices that are not to be re-litigated without new information.

Recorded so they are not re-litigated without new information.

| Decision | Choice | Rejected or noted |
|---|---|---|
| Chat transport | A terminal plus a custom shell | A web API, a tool protocol, and a bus are deferred. The shell is the operator surface. |
| Model SDK | The local-engine starter | Keep a single `LlmService` so a later tool path can reuse prompt assembly. |
| Completion | A blocking call | Streaming and thinking traces are held off because of metadata uncertainty. |
| Context cap | The last N non-system messages | A token-aware window is not built. `message list` is still full. N defaults to 40. |
| Conversation persist | None | Line history is `~/.casserole/history` only. Sessions die with the connection. |
| Escape | Bare Escape after 100 ms | It conflicted with paste and arrows. A timer plus a completeness parser. |
| Command matching | The longest full name | A first-token match broke `chat start`. |
| Command experience | Green echo. Leave `cmd>` after execute. | Command mode is a one-shot line, not a sticky prompt, except the operator can press Escape again. This capture is the one-shot rule. |
| Paste | Bracketed and sealed | Per-line Enter, and a terminal `^C`, made build-file pastes unusable. |
| Load model | HTTP `keep_alive` `-1` | `ollama run` is an interactive prompt. |
| Run the engine binary | Process arguments | No shell command string. Metacharacters are rejected. |
| Spinner default | ASCII. Glyph `#00FF66`. The word `thinking` is `#00D7FF`. | Braille misses glyphs on Consolas. Do not write a committed thinking line. |
| Newlines from the model | Always carriage-return line feed | A lone line feed staircases. |
| Smart format | The first strict detector | No classifier. Identity if unsure. |
| Table chrome | ASCII default | Box drawing can miss glyphs. Configuration can opt into `box`. |
| Assistant color | Bright yellow | User text is white. Command output is the default. Errors are red. |
| Links | The link sequence plus purple. The widget can click. | Opening a browser is a client job. |
| Client auth | Password, and accept every host key | Version 1 proof. |
| Client terminal | Raw. No echo, no canonical mode, no signals. | The server owns the line editor. |
| Font in the paste dialog | Match the spinner and the terminal family | Otherwise the editor looked like the toolkit default. |
| Transparency | Not implemented | Operating-system specific. Outside the pure-runtime scope. |
| Tests | None | Hand check on a plain client and the bundled client. |
| Leftover servers | Keep in the tree for now | `MinimalSshServer` and `SshServerTest` are unused. |
| Web and persistence starter | On the classpath, unused | Later direction. Do not build against them yet. |
| Icon | The dish photograph | Baked into `/icons/casserole.jpg`. |

**Reason.** Each row is a decision that chat history kept re-opening.

## Stage 2 working serial

## The walker

Every send and every inspector preview go through one walker, so the pin cannot lie about the body.

The walker builds the send in this order. The host system line comes first. The default text of that line is `You are the Casserole assistant. Be concise and useful.` The mood system line comes next, when one has been approved. Then the cells, oldest first.

It skips `EXCLUDED`. It skips an empty burner. It honors the four-state role. Collapse stays a view flag and still enters the set.

It resolves `{{cell[k].output}}` on the client, from the cells already in memory, before the frame is built. The host does not fetch the client database.

`k` is the 1-based position in that send order, counting only cells the walker did not skip. The target cell is not a source for itself. The inspector's painted numbers are a different sequence. They are not `k`.

An ephemeral source, a `k` that is not in that sequence, a cycle, or a source that is not a legal body source fails the pipe. A non-empty assistant body stays a source after `CANCELLED`. `FAILED` stops the pipe. The raw braces are not sent to the model. That pipe rule is the approved final shape.

The inspector calls this same walker, then paints the cards newest first. The two system lines stay in a header above the cards, in send order. They are not cards.

The estimate calls `HeuristicTokenCounter` on the text the walker would send, including both system lines. The panel's `length / 4` sum is retired for this view. `HeuristicTokenCounter` uses `(length + 3) / 4`, and an empty string counts as 1.

**Truth.** One walker builds every send and every inspector preview: host system line, approved mood line, then kept cells oldest first. `k` is the 1-based index of kept cells. The host does not fetch the vault. The estimate uses `HeuristicTokenCounter` on that same text.

**Reason.** Two copies of the exclude, burner, and four-state rules are how the inspector starts describing a body the send does not build.

**Avoidances.** Do not keep a second walk for the inspector. Do not use paint order as `k`. Do not let the target be a source for itself. Do not send the raw braces when a pipe fails. Do not drop a non-empty body from the pipe only because the latest status is `CANCELLED`. Do not let a `FAILED` source through. Do not resolve the pipe on the host by reading the client database. Do not retire collapse into `EXCLUDED`.

## Air-gap is enforced where the provider runs

The server is the check that counts, because the provider lives in the host and a frame that skipped the shell still has to fail there.

The server reads `aetheris.network.air-gap` from `~/.aetheris.yaml` through `AetherisYaml`. The shell lookup stays `--aetheris-yaml`, then `./aetheris.yaml`, then `~/.aetheris.yaml`. Those are not one shared file. The shell uses its copy for an early banner and for the status word. `SessionFacts` on `TYPE_INIT` echoes the server value. A mismatch paints the status line and the shell does not send a cloud execute. The server still enforces its own value.

Air-gap true plus a cloud target returns `TYPE_ERROR` and does not call `complete`. The stored target is not rewritten. The banner text is the air-gap banner. A local target whose engine is down returns a different banner. That failure is engine-down.

A missing key loads as `unset`. `unset` refuses cloud. Explicit `false` allows cloud. Explicit `true` refuses cloud. The constitution sample still says `false` when the key is written. This lock does not rewrite that file.

An ephemeral cell plus a cloud target fails the cell while `burner-key` is unset. The constitution phrase stays allow-cloud-burner. The file key is `burner-key`, under the `notebook` root. A bare key does not load. A missing key means deny. The walker omits ephemeral text from a cloud working set. The execute body carries `ephemeral: true` when the target cell is a burner, and the server repeats the deny before `complete`. Local `ollama` still receives burner text. The refuse is the cloud hop. The local base is `http://localhost:11434`.

The status line gains the parsed air-gap word beside vault mode and the engine. The word does not replace the server check.

**Truth.** The server reads `aetheris.network.air-gap` from `~/.aetheris.yaml`. Missing is `unset`, and `unset` refuses cloud. Explicit `false` allows cloud. Explicit `true` refuses cloud. A mismatch blocks the shell's cloud send and the server still enforces its own value. A burner reaches the cloud only when `burner-key` allows it. Missing denies.

**Reason.** A flag that is parsed and never consulted lets a cloud target leave after the operator set the switch. A missing server key must not mean allow, or the shell switch the operator already set is inert.

**Avoidances.** Do not treat the shell file and `~/.aetheris.yaml` as one file. Do not rewrite the stored target when the check fails. Do not use the air-gap banner for engine-down. Do not treat `unset` as `false`. Do not load a bare `burner-key`. Do not send burner text on the cloud hop. Do not let the status word replace the server check. Do not rewrite the constitution sample.

## System is a role, and the host line is visible

The wire role `system` is a system message, and the host line and the mood line stay two visible system messages.

`system` becomes a system message. `user` becomes a user message. `assistant` becomes an assistant message. Any other role fails the cell. It is not stored as something the operator said.

The host line stays the host `chat.system-prompt`. The default text is `You are the Casserole assistant. Be concise and useful.` The mood line is a second system message, added only after approve, and only when a shaper is configured. The two lines are not fused into one string.

The mood dialog stays a `JDialog` on `AetherisWorker`. It is not the interface thread. It is not the host lane. It is not a canvas cell. It is not the terminal tab. Cancel adds no mood line. Approve hands one system line to the walker. That line is not written into a cell body. The inspector header shows it. The skip text stays `keyword only.`

The shaper id, the air-gap skip, and the unreachable skip stay as already locked. The file key is `mood-shape`, under the `notebook` root. It holds the shaper model id. A bare key does not load. An empty id is still the local model in use. The published default for that code model is `qwen2.5-coder:7b`. The local base is `http://localhost:11434`.

**Truth.** Only `system`, `user`, and `assistant` are legal roles. Any other role fails the cell. The host line and the mood line are two system messages, host line first, shown in the inspector header and not written into a cell body.

## Air-gap and the burner

Air-gap is `aetheris.network.air-gap`, and a burner refuses a push, an export body, and a cloud target unless `burner-key` allows the cloud hop.

The constitution sample default, when the key is written, is `false`. A missing key is not that default. A missing key loads as `unset`. `unset` refuses cloud. Explicit `false` allows cloud. Explicit `true` refuses cloud.

Burner execute stays in RAM, paints the interface, and persists metadata and traces with NULL payloads.

It refuses a push. It refuses an export body. It refuses a cloud target unless `burner-key` allows it. The constitution phrase stays allow-cloud-burner. The file key is `burner-key`, under the `notebook` root. A bare key does not load. A missing key means deny.

Heap drop is best-effort. A `String` is not erasable. Ghost, delete, and burner stay three verbs: state, purge, and pin.

Once a payload is sent to a cloud model, it has left the sovereignty boundary.

The server reads `aetheris.network.air-gap` from `~/.aetheris.yaml` through `AetherisYaml`. The shell reads the same key from its own lookup. The status line shows the word beside vault mode and the engine. `SessionFacts` carries the value. A mismatch blocks the shell's cloud send. The server enforces its own value. The stored target is not rewritten.

**Truth.** Missing air-gap is `unset` and refuses cloud. Explicit `false` allows it. Explicit `true` refuses it. A burner keeps NULL payloads, refuses push and export, and reaches a cloud target only when `burner-key` is set. Missing denies.

**Reason.** A payload that has already been sent cannot be pulled back, and a missing key that meant allow would ignore the switch the operator set.

**Avoidances.** Do not treat `unset` as the sample `false`. Do not erase a `String` and call that a secure drop. Do not collapse ghost, delete, and burner into one verb. Do not export a burner body by default. Do not let a burner push. Do not send burner text on the cloud hop when the key is missing. Do not rewrite the constitution phrase or the sample file.

# The longest command name wins, there is no bare chat command, and a finished command leaves command mode.

`CommandProcessor.execute`:

1. Normalize: trim, collapse whitespace, lowercase.
2. The longest registered name or alias that equals the line, or is a prefix followed by a space, wins.
3. The remainder, trimmed, is the arguments.
4. An unknown line prints `Unknown command: …` in red.

This is why multi-word commands work. `chat start`, `message list`, and `ollama load` do not let `start` become arguments of a fictional `chat` command. There is no `chat` command.

Commands are constructed in the factory in this order:

| Name | Aliases | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `chat start` | | Reset the session, active, and the line `Chat session started.` |
| `chat stop` | | Stop the session, idle, history kept |
| `help` | `?` | The catalog, or `help` plus a name for the long text and the aliases |
| `message list` | `messages` | Dump. Filter `all`, the default, or `user`, `assistant`, or `system` |
| `clear` | `history clear` | Drop turns, keep the system message |
| `status` | | Active or idle, mode, shell user, model, and counts |
| `exit` | `quit` | `Goodbye.` and request exit |
| `ollama load` | `ollama start` | HTTP `keep_alive` `-1` |
| `ollama stop` | | Command-line unload |
| `ollama` | | Remaining arguments to the command line |

# The first matching detector wins, a miss is identity plus line endings and links, and detectors are boolean.

`FormatRouter.format` takes the raw text and the context.

1. Empty input yields an empty result with body color applied.
2. Otherwise try handlers in registration order. The first detector that matches wins.
3. Renderer output goes through line endings to carriage-return line feed, a trailing carriage-return line feed, then link annotation.
4. No match uses the same line endings and links on the original text. That is identity. Do not invent a format.

`smart-format: false` registers zero handlers, so the path is always identity, line endings, and links.

Detectors are boolean and strict. No scores. No "probably markdown." The default of the flag is true.

**Truth.** Order is registration order. Empty still asks for body color. False smart-format means no handlers.

**Reason.** A score would format prose the operator did not mark.

**Avoidances.** Do not score. Do not invent a format. Do not skip line endings when smart format is off.

# The order is structured data, fence, table, list, then markdown, and a table turns body color off.

1. Structured data. A whole-string object or array. Scalars do not match. Pretty-print. No wrap. Body color on.
2. Fence. A matching opener and closer of three backticks or three tildes. Prose is wrapped. Fence interiors are untouched. Body color on.
3. Table. A whole-blob pipe table: a header, a separator of dashes or aligned dashes, at least one data row, and equal column counts. Drawn as ASCII or a Unicode box. Body color is off. Borders are electric blue. Cells are yellow through the format context.
4. List. Every non-empty line is a bullet of `-`, `*`, or `+`, or an ordered item of `1.` or `1)`. At least two items. Rendered as a hanging `- ` with wrap at columns minus 2. Body color on.
5. Markdown. The parsed tree has a heading, a fenced code block, a block quote, or a list of at least two items. A single paragraph, even with emphasis markers, does not match. The renderer drops emphasis markers, keeps structure, wraps prose, renders lists as `- `, quotes as `> `, and leaves fenced code literal. Body color on.

**Truth.** Five handlers in that order. Tables paint themselves. A single emphasized paragraph is not markdown.

**Reason.** Tables have to win before the markdown handler, or a pipe table becomes prose.

**Avoidances.** Do not let a scalar match structured data. Do not wrap a fence interior. Do not match a one-item list. Do not match a single paragraph as markdown.

**semantic-key:** PK-5617

# Line endings always become carriage-return line feed, wrap splits only inside structured renderers, and links are purple with an operating-system link when the terminal supports it.

Line endings:

- A lone line feed becomes carriage return plus line feed.
- An existing pair is kept.
- A lone carriage return becomes the pair.
- A trailing pair is ensured.

This is the staircase fix. It runs even when smart format is off.

Wrap:

- Hard wrap at spaces. An overlong token is split.
- Used by structured renderers only, never by identity, so preformatted structured data or code on the identity path is not smashed. The structured-data handler also does not wrap.

Links:

- Finds `http://` and `https://`.
- Skips the blob if it already contains an operating-system command link, or if the URL contains a carriage return or a line feed.
- Wraps with purple, then the link sequence `ESC]8;;` plus the URL plus the bell, then the URL, then the closing link sequence, then reset.
- Trims a trailing period, comma, semicolon, or closing bracket.
- Stops the URL at whitespace and at `<`, `>`, quotes, apostrophe, and `)`.

The terminal widget also has its own URL highlighter. The hyperlink color is purple `rgb(180, 80, 255)`. A click uses the widget's open-as-URL action, which asks the desktop to browse. The link sequence is for capable terminals. The purple color is the visual even if that sequence is ignored.

**Truth.** Always CRLF. Wrap only in structured renderers. Purple links. Hyperlink color `rgb(180, 80, 255)`. Trailing punctuation trimmed.

**Reason.** Identity wrap would smash a structured payload, and a lone line feed staircases.

**Avoidances.** Do not wrap the identity path. Do not wrap structured data. Do not annotate a URL that already has a link sequence or that contains a line break.

The format context from the shell carries columns from the terminal, the table style from configuration, an electric-blue border, a yellow header and cell, and reset.

## Edges, bottlenecks, and failure modes

These edges are how the floor fails when more than one cell runs, and a plan has to name each one before the row that hits it is built.

1. The model slot and the lane pool. The host engine gives `LLM_EXEC` four threads. The terminal chat and a notebook execute share that pool. The local engine's default is one request at a time. Four lane threads can sit inside `complete` while one HTTP call owns the model. A fifth model task waits on the pool. Stop cancels the host handle. An HTTP call that ignores the interrupt still holds the slot until it returns. That fact is already recorded for one call.
